study_identification_part.si4_title: A 10-Year Longitudinal Study of Brain Cortical Thickness in People with FirstEpisode Psychosis Using Normative Models

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Characterize 10-year longitudinal trajectories of cortical thickness deviations in first-episode psychosis and test associations between deviation scores and symptoms (PANSS).

rci1_dataset_name.answer: Multi-site aggregated datasets (77 sites; mostly public) for reference normative models; TOP (controls) used for local adaptation
rci1_dataset_name.reason: The paper states the reference normative models were trained on pooled, mostly public datasets from 77 sites (N=40,435) and then adapted to three TOP scanners using held-out controls. Specific dataset names are not listed.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: "Using pooled data from a collection of mostly publicly available datasets from 77 sites, and 40 435 participants ... We then adapted the model to the 3 unseen Oslo scanners ... For this adaptation step, we used held-out cross-sectional data from CTRL from these 3 scanners"

rci2_hc_n.reason: Table 1 reports N=218 healthy controls included at baseline in the longitudinal analysis.

rci3_hc_age.answer: mean 33.90; sd 10.10; min NR; max NR
rci3_hc_age.reason: Baseline age for CTRL is reported as 33.9 [10.1] in Table 1. Range is not reported.

rci4_hc_sex.reason: CTRL female percentage at baseline is 42.6%. With total N=218, we computed counts by multiplying and rounding to nearest integer (F≈93; M=218-93=125).

rci5_imaging_modality.reason: The study acquires T1-weighted structural MRI and models cortical thickness.
rci5_imaging_modality.supporting_text: "T1-weighted structural MRI scans were preprocessed ... CT measures were parcellated ..."; "T1-weighted images were acquired ..."

rci6_analysis_level.supporting_text: "We estimated a normative model for each region of interest (ROI, n = 150) in the Freesurfer Destrieux atlas"

rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.answer: FreeSurfer v5.3; Destrieux atlas parcellation (150 ROIs); automated QC via FreeSurfer Euler characteristic (>5 removed)
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.reason: Preprocessing uses FreeSurfer 5.3 with Destrieux parcellation and an Euler-number-based QC threshold.
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.supporting_text: "T1-weighted structural MRI scans were preprocessed through Freesurfer (version 5.3), and CT measures were parcellated using the Destrieux atlas. An automatic quality check procedure based on the Freesurfer Euler characteristic was run on all data and samples with a value higher than 5 were removed."

rci8_quality_checking.detail: Automated QC using FreeSurfer Euler characteristic; subjects with Euler > 5 excluded (threshold specified).
rci8_quality_checking.supporting_text: "An automatic quality check procedure based on the Freesurfer Euler characteristic was run on all data and samples with a value higher than 5 were removed."

rci9_site_effect_handling.detail: Hierarchical Bayesian regression with sex and scanner ID as batch effects; transfer learning adaptation to 3 local scanners using held-out controls; multi-site pooling across 77 sites.
rci9_site_effect_handling.supporting_text: "we used the Hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) approach for normative modeling ... using HBR with age as a covariate, and sex and scanner id as batch effects ... This accommodated multisite pooling using transfer learning ... We then adapted the model to the 3 unseen Oslo scanners ... using held-out cross-sectional data from CTRL"

nm1_model_origin.detail: Pre-trained HBR on pooled multi-site datasets (N=40,435; 77 sites; 95% healthy); adapted to TOP scanners via transfer learning with local controls (held-out).
nm1_model_origin.supporting_text: "Using pooled data from a collection of mostly publicly available datasets from 77 sites, and 40 435 participants ... trained on (95%) healthy individuals and validated on an independent set ... We then adapted the model to the 3 unseen Oslo scanners ... using held-out ... CTRL"

nm2_modeling_method.reason: Explicitly stated as the normative modeling approach used to predict cortical thickness per ROI.
nm2_modeling_method.supporting_text: "we used the Hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) approach for normative modeling"

nm3_software_tool.reason: The manuscript and supplement do not specify software packages or libraries used to implement HBR (e.g., PCNtoolkit/Stan).
nm3_software_tool.supporting_text: No explicit mention of software/tool for normative modeling was found.

nm4_response_variable.answer: Cortical thickness per ROI (Destrieux atlas; 150 ROIs)
nm4_response_variable.reason: Normative models per ROI predict cortical thickness values based on age, sex, and scanner id.
nm4_response_variable.supporting_text: "We estimated a normative model for each region of interest (ROI, n = 150) ... to predict CT."

nm5_predictor_variables.reason: Stated as covariate and batch variables in the HBR normative models.
nm5_predictor_variables.supporting_text: "using HBR with age as a covariate, and sex and scanner id as batch effects, to predict CT"

nm6_predictor_effects.answer: Age = fixed (covariate); Sex/Scanner = batch with site-specific random effects (HBR piecewise linear trajectories)
nm6_predictor_effects.reason: HBR includes batch effects and fits site-specific intercepts and slopes, implying random effects across sites/scanners.
nm6_predictor_effects.supporting_text: "using HBR with age as a covariate, and sex and scanner id as batch effects ... Importantly, as HBR fits site-specific intercepts and slopes, the resulting normative trajectory might not be linear across the lifespan, but rather piecewise linear."

nm7_nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The approach addresses site/scanner (batch) via HBR and transfer learning; accounts for age effects; includes QC. The deviations are validated and used in LMEs with nuisance covariates handled.
nm7_nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: "we used the HBR approach ... sex and scanner id as batch effects ... multisite pooling using transfer learning ... We defined the threshold for extreme deviation values as |z| > 2.0"

nm8_nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: Normative parameters were not evaluated on the same training data without independence; reference models used a 95/5 split and adaptation used held-out controls.
nm8_nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: "... trained on (95%) healthy individuals and validated on an independent set of 2548 ..."

nm9_nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The reference models were validated on an independent 5% set (stratified by sites).
nm9_nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.supporting_text: "... validated on an independent set of 2548 CTRL and patients (5%, stratified by sites)"

nm10_nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: Models trained on external multi-site datasets were adapted and applied to TOP (unseen Oslo scanners), constituting different-domain application.
nm10_nm_vldtn_diff_domain.supporting_text: "We then adapted the model to the 3 unseen Oslo scanners ... After this transfer step, we tested the normative models on the remaining longitudinal CTRL and SCZ samples"

caa1_clinical_dataset.supporting_text: "within the Thematically Organized Psychosis (TOP) study"; "We then adapted the model to the 3 unseen Oslo scanners ... tested ... on the remaining longitudinal CTRL and SCZ samples"

caa6_deviation_metric.answer: Z-score deviations per ROI; extreme defined as |z| > 2.0
caa6_deviation_metric.reason: Explicit threshold for extreme deviations is specified; deviations are per-ROI z-scores from normative models.
caa6_deviation_metric.supporting_text: "We defined the threshold for extreme deviation values as | z | > 2.0"

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Linear mixed effects models linking ROI-wise deviation scores with PANSS (total and domains), with covariates (age, sex, time) and FDR correction; group/time interactions tested; t-tests and Wilcoxon tests for group differences and extreme deviation proportions.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: CT deviations in patients attenuate over 10 years; ACC deviations relate to PANSS total, and insular/orbitofrontal deviations to PANSS negative scores.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: LMEs showed conditional main effects of diagnosis and time×diagnosis in a distributed network; baseline median CT deviation d≈-0.46, at 12 months d≈-0.43, at 10 years d≈-0.27; no significant CTRL–SCZ deviation differences at 10 years; associations: anterior cingulate with PANSS total, insula and orbitofrontal with PANSS negative; normative deviations enable cross-scanner comparisons and suggest attenuation rather than progressive worsening.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Potential recruitment/retention biases; limited first-generation antipsychotic exposure; extreme deviations may reflect confounds; moderate sample size at 10-year follow-up; different scanners across waves may influence findings.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: "ensuring representative recruitment ... or bias on the selection of healthy subjects ... retention ..."; "only a very small number of participants were taking first-generation antipsychotics"; "extreme cortical deviations may ... be markers of other effects ... While we cannot rule out confounding effects ..."; "our sample size at the third follow-up session is moderate ... inclusion of different scanners across different waves ... may have influenced our findings"

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Transfer learning from large-scale reference normative models enabled cross-scanner longitudinal comparisons within TOP; adaptation used held-out local controls on three scanners (TOP15, TOP3T, TOP3T-GE).

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: Reference normative datasets are described as mostly publicly available but not itemized; adaptation sample characteristics for the three local scanners are in Supplementary Table 1 (CTRL-only). Software for HBR implementation not specified.
